title: the Free Port Rising Anew
premise: Ivo Yarrow, a financial-crimes investigator whose career is built on laundering the reputations of the untouchable, is handed a dead-end case: a private jet that took off from the Free Port of Meridian and never landed anywhere, its flight record erased mid-air. Digging into the vanished flight, Ivo uncovers a slush fund that three governments use to move money and people off the books—and discovers their own name on the passenger manifest of a flight they never took, a forged identity designed to make them the perfect fall person for an assassination scheduled to happen at the Meridian summit. Hunted by the assassin sent to close the loop and betrayed by the mentor who built the forgery, Ivo must smuggle the ledger of the vanished flight past three intelligence services to a journalist who may be the only honest person left. In the end, Ivo chooses truth over survival: the ledger goes public, the summit collapses, the mentor dies protecting them, and Ivo walks out of the Free Port with a new name of their own choosing—visible at last.
about_author: Astrid Okafor is a former compliance auditor who spent six years tracing money through free ports before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers from a harbourside flat in Lagos, where the cargo cranes never stop moving.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Ivo Yarrow's POV. Ivo scrubs a corrupt minister's finances so thoroughly the scandal dies in a news cycle, then goes home to an apartment with no photos and a phone that never rings with real names. The emotional beat is the quiet hollowness of a life built to leave no trace.

chapters.title: The Case Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo's mentor, Director Sable Voss, hands over a file with no attribution: a charter jet, tail number Vesper-9, departed the Free Port of Meridian and has no arrival record in any of forty databases. The emotional beat is professional curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Forty Databases, Zero Landings
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with the assassin Kirin watching Meridian harbor. Ivo confirms the erasure happened while the plane was airborne—someone with treaty-level access killed the flight in real time. The beat is the first vertigo of realizing the case is bigger than a cover-up.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In a corrupted customs archive Ivo finds the passenger list—and their own name, date of birth, and a biometric hash that matches, on a flight Ivo never took. The beat is cold fear: someone has been building a second Ivo Yarrow for years.

chapters.title: What the Free Port Keeps
chapters.summary: Kirin's POV. Kirin arrives in Meridian under a trade-delegation cover, reviewing a kill list that includes a name Ivo Yarrow and a date: the summit, eleven days out. The beat is chilling competence; Kirin is not hunting Ivo yet, only preparing the frame.

chapters.title: Sable's Lesson
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV with a flashback to Voss training them years ago: 'Attribution is a weapon; learn to hold the wrong end.' Ivo confronts Voss about the manifest and gets a warning to drop the case. The beat is loyalty strained against a first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Vesper-9
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the jet's fuel payments, Ivo finds a shell company whose books record not just money but people—diplomats, defectors, witnesses—moved off the books by three governments. The beat is awe curdling into horror at the machinery.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo approaches Nadia Ferro, a disgraced journalist who once burned a source to survive, now working a kiosk archive in the old port. Their first conversation is barbed, but she recognizes the ledger's signature. The beat is two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Intelligence officers from three nations each quietly open a file on the same anomaly—Vesper-9—and each concludes Ivo Yarrow is either an asset or a problem. The beat is the noose tightening from directions Ivo can't see.

chapters.title: The Tail Number
chapters.summary: Kirin's POV. Kirin traces the same fuel-paper trail and realizes someone else is reading the ledger; orders come down to accelerate. Kirin stages a break-in at Ivo's apartment—not to steal, but to leave fingerprints. The beat is dread: the frame is being assembled.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo's credentials are revoked, accounts frozen, and an Interpol flag appears under their name citing the vanished flight. Voss offers one lifeline: confess to negligence and disappear. The beat is betrayal crystallizing—Voss built the false Ivo.

chapters.title: Run the Money, Run the City
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using launderer's tradecraft against the system that taught it, Ivo moves through Meridian's cash economy—chandler's bunks, ferry crews, prepaid everything—while Nadia copies the ledger. The beat is grim exhilaration: invisibility as a skill, finally theirs.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia decodes the ledger's passenger entries and finds Vesper-9 carried a witness—a Meridian port clerk who could testify to the fund—whose death was ruled an accident last spring. The beat is grief and resolve: this is no longer abstract.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Kirin's POV. Kirin finally meets Ivo face to face in a fish-market crowd, not to kill but to verify the fall person exists and looks the part. A strange, almost respectful exchange leaves Kirin doubting the file for the first time. The beat is the assassin's first fracture.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornering Voss at a harbor chapel, Ivo learns the truth: Voss created the false identity years ago as insurance, and the summit assassination is the price three governments agreed to pay to bury Vesper-9. Voss begs Ivo to run. The beat is love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and Kirin POV. Ivo and Nadia plan to move the ledger out through the port's grain inspection channel; Kirin is ordered to kill Ivo before the summit and finds themselves slow-walking the hunt. The beat is a ticking clock and a hunter losing conviction.

chapters.title: The Grain Ship
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The ledger's first copy leaves aboard a grain ship—but one of the three services intercepts the courier, and now all three know Ivo has a second copy. The beat is a trap snapping half-shut: victory and catastrophe in the same hour.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Kirin's POV. On the eve of the summit, Kirin is given the final go order and the full truth of the frame—and chooses, for the first time in a career of certainty, not to obey. The beat is the assassin's defection, quiet and irreversible.

chapters.title: The Kill Floor
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Voss, exposed as the ledger's architect, is executed by the fund's protectors to close the loop; Ivo finds the body and Voss's last message pointing to the summit's broadcast hub. The beat is devastating grief converted into purpose.

chapters.title: Meridian, Day One
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. During the summit's opening session, Ivo and Kirin—assassin and target, now reluctant allies—fight through the hub's security while Nadia holds the last copy. The beat is the climax's white heat: trust built in gunfire.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. From the hub, Nadia pushes the Vesper-9 ledger to every wire service at once; the summit collapses mid-session, delegations walk out, and the three services' cover story burns in public. The beat is catharsis—truth arriving too loud to bury.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, weeks later. Investigations bloom, Kirin vanishes into a new life with a debt unpaid, and Ivo—cleared but changed—registers a name for the first time: not the forged one, not the invisible one, but one chosen. The beat is resolution: identity reclaimed, love and loss carried forward.
